key_insight: β-TeO3 is predicted to be a wide-gap n-type semiconductor with an exceptionally high work function, reaching about 8 eV.
engineering_relevance: Its combination of ultrahigh work function and wide band gap makes it promising for hole-injection/transport layers and transparent electrodes in optoelectronic and photovoltaic devices.
method: First-principles calculations of electronic structure and defect energetics
Assessment of point defects and impurities, including H, Li, Na, Cu, Mg, Zn, F, and O vacancies
Work-function evaluation across multiple low-index nonpolar surfaces
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a band gap above 3 eV, shallow donor behavior for several impurities, and surface-dependent work functions approaching ~8 eV.
watch_item: Surface O-vacancy formation can lower the work function, so strict control of oxygen chemical potential and surface stoichiometry is critical.
paper_title: Tellurium trioxide as an n-type wide-gap semiconductor with ultrahigh work functions from first principles
